'''Michael Kneissl''' is a German [[physicist]] and professor at the Institute of [[Solid-state physics|Solid State Physics]] at [[Technische Universität Berlin]].

Kneissl received his [[Dr. rer. nat.|doctoral degree]] in physics from the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg|Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]] in 1996.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://d-nb.info/95103216X |title=Elektroabsorption in Quantentopfstrukturen unter dem Einfluß schichtparalleler elektrischer Felder und deren Anwendung in elektrooptischen Modulatoren |series=Physik mikrostrukturierter Halbleiter |year=1997 |publisher=German National Library |isbn=9783932392030 |language=de |accessdate=2022-05-28}}</ref> During his graduate studies, he was a visiting scholar at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1993. He joined the [[PARC (company)|Xerox Palo Alto Research Center (PARC)]] in 1996. Since 2005, he has been a [[Full Professor]] and the Chair of Experimental [[Nanophysics]] & [[Photonics]] at the TU Berlin.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://idw-online.de/en/news124091|title=Personalia der TU Berlin|publisher=Informationsdienst Wissenschaft|language=de|accessdate=2021-11-21}}</ref> He holds a joint appointment at the [[Ferdinand-Braun-Institut]] in Berlin, where he heads the Joint Lab [[GaN]]-[[Optoelectronics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fbh-berlin.de/en/about-us/structure/labs-departments/photonics/joint-lab-gan-optoelectronics|title=Joint Lab GaN Optoelectronics|publisher=Ferdinand-Braun-Institut|accessdate=2021-11-22}}</ref> Excluding a two-year hiatus in 2021 he has served as the Executive Director of the Institute of Solid State Physics at TU Berlin from 2011 to 2025. Since 2021 Kneissl is the Chairman of the Executive Board of the [https://www.advanced-uv.de Advanced UV for Life e.V.] association and since 2024 spokesperson for the newly established [https://www.tu.berlin/en/naturwissenschaften/ciphor Center for Integrated Photonics Research (CIPHOR)] at TU Berlin. 

His research interests include [[Boron group|group III]]-nitride semiconductor materials, [[metalorganic vapour-phase epitaxy]] of [[wide-bandgap semiconductor]]s and ([[Indium gallium nitride|In]])[[Aluminium gallium nitride|AlGaN]] nanostructures as well as novel optoelectronic devices, including [[Ultraviolet|UV]] [[Ultraviolet LED|LEDs]] and [[Ultraviolet#Ultraviolet lasers|laser diodes]].<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v14/120 |title=Zapping Germs with LEDs |journal=Physics |date=31 August 2021 |volume=14 |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |accessdate=2022-05-28|last1=Schirber |first1=Michael |page=120 |doi=10.1103/Physics.14.120 |bibcode=2021PhyOJ..14..120S |s2cid=244180585 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021/02/f82/ssl-rd21-kneissl-uv-led.pdf |title=Advances & Challenges for AlGaN-based UV-LED technologies |publisher=[[United States Department of Energy]] |accessdate=2022-05-28}}</ref>

He was named [[Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) in 2016<ref>{{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203191938/http://www.ieee.org/membership_services/membership/fellows/2016_elevated_fellows.pdf|title=2016 elevated fellow|website=IEEE Fellows Directory|date=2017-02-03}}</ref> ''for contributions to the development of wide bandgap semiconductor laser diodes and ultraviolet LEDs''. He holds more than 60 patents in the area of group III-nitride device technologies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/michael-kneissl |title=Patents by Inventor Michael Kneissl |publisher=Justia Inc. |accessdate=2022-05-28}}</ref>
